ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices $B$, $C$ of rectangle $ABCD$ are on the positive x-axis, with $AB=8$ and $BC=6$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}(x>0)$ passes through point $E$ and intersects $AB$ and $CD$ at points $F$ and $G$, respectively. If $OC=10$, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[
\textbf{Solution:} \quad \text{Given that in rectangle ABCD, AB = 8, BC = 6, and OC = 10,} \\
\therefore OB = OC - BC = 4, \\
\therefore B(4,0), A(4,8), C(10,0), \\
\text{since diagonals AC and BD intersect at point E,} \\
\therefore \text{point E is the midpoint of AC,} \\
\therefore E(7,4), \\
\text{substituting } E(7,4) \text{ into } y = \frac{k}{x} \text{ gives } k = 7 \times 4 = \boxed{28}.
\]
